horizon_blocks.base_case: The next weekly EIA release can test whether the small refill persisted; weather and a pre-release consensus are required to distinguish seasonality from a tradable surprise. If independent balance evidence confirms tightening, upward pressure is possible; warmer weather or supply recovery can reverse it. No price target or probability is estimated.

owner_summary.current_thesis: Capital Chronicle analysis: the smaller seasonal refill tightens the weekly balance at the margin, while the above-average stock cushion limits a simple shortage interpretation. It does not measure a market surprise or predict the CFD price.
owner_summary.what_changed: EIA release 2026-10-15: the weekly injection was 67 Bcf for the week ended 2026-10-09, versus the five-year same-week injection average of 90 Bcf. The stock level was 3567 Bcf, 45 Bcf above the five-year stock average and 143 Bcf below the prior-year stock level.

public_safe_claims.basis_risk: Underlying evidence does not establish executable CFD economics.

supporting_evidence.source_identity: U.S. EIA Form EIA-912 / Weekly Natural Gas Storage Report Supplement
